c8_decomposition.reading: c8 predates 5fb2c140 (2026-10-27), which taught this block to reuse the step's own velocity prediction. Until then the adapter was called with include_fm_term=True and returned fm_loss + p_self*shortcut_mse, i.e. the main FM MSE entered the objective a SECOND time. The ratio of 1.00 to within 3% at three consecutive epochs is the signature of a duplicate; the shortcut term's own contribution is the excess.

honest_limits: The excess in c8_decomposition is exact only up to the dropout difference between the two forwards: the field carries egnn_context_dropout 0.1, and the pre-fix code recomputed the FM MSE rather than reusing the step's own. The ratio argument does not depend on this — a duplicate tracks fm_term regardless of dropout.

The 46.3 / 43.9 / 42.4 'on-self MSE' figure quoted in an earlier reading of c8 was WRONG: it assumed include_fm_term=False. The correct implied shortcut_mse is 0.0824 / 0.2584 / 0.4814. The earlier figure is retracted here rather than deleted from the record.

Two structural defects in the term itself are documented at launch and NOT fixed: (1) shortcut_pair builds x_s at flow time tau = t + s(1-t) but labels it s (200k uniform (t,s), seed 0: mean |tau-s| = 0.2493, max 0.9990, 15.17% off by more than 0.5; the perpendicular deviation of x_s from the flow line is 5.4e-8, so the state is right and the label is wrong); (2) the 1-p_self share of the batch is scored at (x_t, t) against the step's own prediction, so that half measures dropout variance and can never reach zero while dropout is on. Fixing either changes what the archived c7/c8 runs mean, and neither can be validated without a training run.
No GPU run. Nothing here says whether the weighted term helps or hurts; it only says the term can now be scaled, is live, and was never 100% of the objective.
